title: Config-change curator: delta-driven canonical corpus workflow and ACL-managed snapshots
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a delta-driven corpus curator service and snapshot workflow that ties config/model changes to targeted re-evals while enforcing team-scoped ACLs and immutable snapshots. Motivation: current practice requires ad-hoc full re-evals or manual curator intervention when model/config rollout occurs; this leads to noisy signals, slow feedback, and unclear ownership. Scope: 1) corpus-curator microservice that computes change deltas from signed canonical snapshots; 2) ledger of snapshot hashes + signer metadata; 3) config-change webhooks that map to corpus selectors and trigger either partial re-evals (affected prompts only) or dry-run canaries; 4) ACLs at dataset and prompt-bundle granularity and UI hooks for Console to request review/approval; 5) integration with existing eval-orchestration (ENG-41123) to schedule replays and capture regression metrics. Out of scope: full dataset migration tooling and automated prompt rewriting tools.
acceptance_criteria: corpus-curator service exposes an API to register canonical snapshots and returns stable hash IDs
config-change webhook can be registered in runtime config and produces a delta list of affected prompt IDs within 60s
snapshots are stored in S3 with versioned prefixes and signer metadata; replay controller can fetch snapshot by hash ID
team-scoped ACLs enforced: only curators or owners in ACL can promote a snapshot to 'trusted' for gating re-rollouts
CI gating: changes cause a canary re-eval job that runs on a sampled subset; rollback flag can be set automatically if F1/accuracy regressions exceed configured thresholds
end-to-end demo documented with links to Confluence design and a staging dashboard showing per-prompt delta comparisons
comments: 2025-02-14 - Triage note (Ava Chen): scoped ticket after sync with PM. Decided to prioritize per-prompt deltas over full diffs to reduce compute cost for large corpora.

2025-02-20 - Architecture sync (Liam Patel): proposed ledger model (hash + signer + timestamp) vs storing full diffs. Trade-off: ledger + object storage is simpler and safer for immutability; full diffs are heavier for complex restructuring. Agreed on ledger+storage approach.

2025-02-24 - Design review (with PM & Security): PM suggested including curator approval flows for 'trusted' snapshots. Security flagged signer rotation and KMS integration; assigned follow-up to ENG-73183 for KMS integration.

links: PM spec: PM-14201 (prompt-bundle ACLs and signatures)
implementation_notes: Service: corpus-curator (Go) behind internal API gateway. Data model: snapshot_record {id, s3_prefix, hash, signer_id, created_by, created_at, state}. Deltas computed by comparing prompt IDs + fingerprint (sha256 of prompt string + metadata) between upstream snapshot and current source. Re-eval scheduler receives delta list and schedules jobs via existing eval-orch queue. Use Cloud KMS to store signer public keys and support rotation. ACLs backed by Console user groups and RBAC service.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Incremental re-evals greatly reduce cost but risk missing systemic regressions if snapshot selection is too narrow. To mitigate, we will run periodic full-sweep re-evals on a cadence (weekly) and require 'trusted' snapshots to pass a regression threshold. Storing only hashes + objects reduces database bloat but requires reliable S3 retention policies and cross-region replication for durability.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): register snapshots and compute deltas only; owners manually trigger re-evals. Phase 2 (beta): allow canary re-eval jobs on config-change webhooks for a subset of customers. Phase 3 (GA): enable automatic gating for selected runtime configs with rollback on regression. UI: Console -> Data -> Curator -> Snapshot details -> Promote to trusted (requires approver).
